content: Calcium iodide (CaI₂) is an ionic compound composed of calcium and iodine. It is highly soluble in water and exhibits deliquescent properties, meaning it can absorb moisture from the air and dissolve in it. At room temperature, calcium iodide exists as a solid and behaves as a typical ionic halide. Due to its hygroscopic nature, it must be stored in tightly sealed containers to prevent it from absorbing moisture from the environment. In many ways, calcium iodide shares similarities with calcium chloride. One of its applications is in the field of photography. Henri Moissan was the first to isolate pure calcium metal by reducing calcium iodide with pure sodium metal. Calcium iodide can also be synthesized by reacting calcium carbonate with hydroiodic acid. Over time, calcium iodide reacts slowly with oxygen and carbon dioxide in the air, leading to the release of free iodine.
